fundamentals.title: Programming fundamentals
fundamentals.description: Languages, complexity, and solving simple problems.

steps.title: Variables and input/output
steps.description: Learn data types, conditions, loops, and standard input/output.

steps.title: Arrays and strings
steps.description: Practice indexing, slices, counting, and string processing.

steps.title: Complexity analysis
steps.description: Estimate time and memory use against problem limits.

steps.title: Sorting and searching
steps.description: Use sorting, binary search, and invariants.

steps.title: Trees and graphs
steps.description: Explore relationships, trees, and graph representations.

steps.title: Segment tree
steps.description: Answer range queries and updates in logarithmic time.

steps.title: Two pointers
steps.description: Process sorted arrays and strings in linear time.

steps.title: Graph traversal
steps.description: Find distances, components, and paths with BFS and DFS.

steps.title: Dynamic programming
steps.description: Define states, transitions, and base cases.

steps.title: Contest practice
steps.description: Reinforce your skills with timed rounds and editorials.

algorithms.title: Algorithms
algorithms.description: Learn core algorithmic techniques and apply them to problems.
algorithms.practiceDescription: Solve related problems to reinforce this technique.

binary-search.title: Binary search
binary-search.description: Finds an answer in a sorted range by halving the search space at each step.
binary-search.example: Find the first matching index in a sorted array.

two-pointers.title: Two pointers
two-pointers.description: Coordinates two indices to solve pair and range problems in linear time.
two-pointers.example: Find a pair with a target sum in a sorted array.

bfs.title: Breadth-first search (BFS)
bfs.description: Traverses a graph layer by layer and finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs.
bfs.example: Minimum number of edges from a source to every vertex.

dfs.title: Depth-first search (DFS)
dfs.description: Explores as far as possible along each branch to detect components and cycles.
dfs.example: Count the connected components of a graph.

dynamic-programming.title: Dynamic programming
dynamic-programming.description: Stores overlapping subproblem results to avoid recalculating them.
dynamic-programming.example: Longest common subsequence or minimum cost.

dijkstra.title: Dijkstra's algorithm
dijkstra.description: Finds shortest paths from one source in graphs with non-negative edge weights.
dijkstra.example: Find the cheapest route on a weighted map.

segment-tree.title: Segment tree
segment-tree.description: Efficiently answers range queries and applies updates to an array.
segment-tree.example: Find a range maximum and update array values.
